---
title: "OSMnx · Basemaps & API textures (La Paz)"
---

::: {.lead}
Drape satellite, street and WMS imagery over the **Avenida Naciones Unidas, La
Paz** terrain. Covers **5 · Basemap Texture** of the
[Elevation panel](../../../panels/osmnx/elevation.qmd) and continues from
[Elevation, DEM & 3D terrain](elevation.qmd).
:::

The basemap controls stay hidden until a terrain object exists, so finish
[Elevation, DEM & 3D terrain](elevation.qmd) first. Blender needs internet access
either way, since the imagery APIs stream tiles or a WMS image.

## 1. Why La Paz

The basemap is fetched for the terrain's geographic bounding box and UV-mapped
onto the mesh, so it follows the elevation surface instead of lying flat. On
gentle terrain that is hard to see. On La Paz's relief the imagery wraps over
ridges and valleys, which makes it easy to confirm the texture is georeferenced
and aligned with the streets.

![The La Paz terrain ready to receive a basemap.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/10-basemap-terrain.png)

## 2. Choose an imagery source

**Source** is grouped by provider, and each provider exposes several styles.

| Provider | Styles | Key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Esri** | Satellite (Imagery), Streets, Topographic, Dark Gray Canvas, Light Gray Canvas, Ocean Base, Hillshade, Terrain Base | None |
| **OpenStreetMap** | OSM Standard, OpenTopoMap | None |
| **CARTO** | Voyager, Positron (Light), Dark Matter | None (fair-use) |
| **Mapbox** | Satellite, Satellite Streets, Streets, Outdoors, Light, Dark | Mapbox token |
| **MapTiler** | Satellite, Satellite Hybrid, Streets, Topographic, Outdoor, Basic, Winter, Ocean | MapTiler key |
| **Stadia / Stamen** | Alidade Smooth (Light), Alidade Smooth Dark, Outdoors, Stamen Toner (B/W), Stamen Terrain, Stamen Watercolor | Stadia key |
| **Custom WMS** | Any OGC WMS `GetMap` layer | Depends on server |

**Esri · Satellite (Imagery)** is the best first pass: high resolution, no key.
The minimal canvas styles (Positron, Dark Matter, Light/Dark Gray) work better as
neutral backdrops for data overlays.

![Selecting an imagery source in the Basemap Texture step.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/10-basemap-source.png)

::: {.callout-note}
Keys go in add-on preferences. Select a key-bound source without its key and the
panel names the provider in a hint and blocks the fetch.
:::

## 3. Set zoom (tile sources)

Every provider except WMS needs a **Zoom**. Higher zoom means more detail and
more tiles, so use the live tile-count estimate to balance the two before
fetching. Very high zoom over the 2 km radius is capped to stop accidental large
requests, and styles with a lower native maximum are clamped automatically.

![The zoom control with the live tile-count estimate.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/10-basemap-zoom.png)

## 4. Fetch and apply

**Fetch & Apply** downloads the tiles (or the single WMS image), stitches them
into one georeferenced image, and drapes it over the terrain with per-vertex UV
mapping. The active source and its attribution appear once it is applied.

![Esri satellite imagery draped over the La Paz terrain.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/10-basemap-esri.png)

::: {.callout-tip}
Fetching is cancellable. Interrupt a long download and in-flight tile requests
are dropped, so Blender's UI does not freeze.
:::

## 5. Use a WMS layer

For an institutional or national orthophoto service, set **Source** to **WMS**
and fill in **WMS URL** and **Layer**. The add-on issues one `GetMap` request in
`EPSG:4326` for the terrain's bounding box, so the returned image maps linearly
onto the mesh.

![A WMS orthophoto layer applied to the terrain.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/10-basemap-wms.png)

## 6. Compare and swap textures

**Clear** removes the current basemap, then fetch a different source to compare
them on the same relief. Downloaded tiles are cached, so re-fetching a source and
zoom you have already used is fast.

![Comparing satellite and street basemaps on the same La Paz terrain.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/10-basemap-compare.png)
